location: Imet Gogo viewpoint, Simien Mountains National Park, Amhara
alt: Rocky pinnacle and escarpment edge at the Imet Gogo viewpoint in the Simien Mountains
caption: The Imet Gogo viewpoint on the Simien escarpment, a UNESCO site of cliffs and pinnacles near Debark. The Simien cliff-edge trek is the trip's main high-mountain walk.

alt: The cross-shaped rock-hewn church of Bete Giyorgis seen from above in its pit
caption: Bete Giyorgis, Lalibela's cross-shaped church carved down into the rock. It is the most famous of the 11 rock-hewn churches and the main reason pilgrims and visitors come to Lalibela.

location: Sanetti Plateau, Bale Mountains National Park, Oromia
alt: High afroalpine moorland of the Sanetti Plateau in the Bale Mountains
caption: The Sanetti Plateau, an afroalpine plateau at around 4,000 m in Bale Mountains National Park. It is the highest-altitude landscape of the southern leg and home to Ethiopian wolves.

commonsFile: File:Old City (Jugal) Street Scene of Jugol 14.jpg
alt: Street scene in the old walled city of Harar Jugol with houses and people
caption: A street in Harar Jugol, the walled Islamic city and UNESCO site in eastern Ethiopia. It is the trip's contrast to the highland Christian north, reached by flight and road transfer.

alt: The stone castle of Emperor Fasilides in the royal enclosure of Gondar
caption: Fasilides' castle in the Fasil Ghebbi royal enclosure of Gondar, a 17th-century Ethiopian imperial capital. It is the secular-history stop between Lalibela and the Simien Mountains.

alt: Coloured sulphur and salt formations at Dallol in the Danakil Depression
caption: The multi-coloured sulphur, salt and iron deposits at Dallol in the Danakil Depression, one of the hottest and lowest places on Earth. It is the most extreme landscape on the route and needs a specialist operator.

alt: Tall carved granite stelae standing in the Stelae Park at Axum
caption: The carved stelae of Axum, monuments of the ancient Aksumite kingdom. They anchor the trip's ancient-civilisation theme in the north.

alt: Sandstone towers of the Gheralta Massif rising above the plain
caption: The sandstone towers of the Gheralta Massif, where rock-hewn churches perch on cliffs and are reached by climbing. It is the adventurous side of Tigray's church heritage.

alt: Cloud forest of the Harenna Forest with the Bale Mountains rising behind
caption: The Harenna cloud forest below the Bale Mountains, reached by descending south from the Sanetti Plateau. It adds a lush, wildlife-rich contrast to the high moorland.

alt: A busy street in the Merkato market district of Addis Ababa
caption: A street in Merkato, Addis Ababa's huge open-air market and one of Africa's largest. It is where the trip starts and ends in everyday Ethiopian city life.

alt: The round church of Betremariam Monastery among trees on Lake Tana
caption: Betremariam, one of the old Orthodox monasteries on Lake Tana. Boat trips from Bahir Dar to the island monasteries are the lake's main cultural draw.

commonsFile: File:Ethiopian wolf, Sanetti Plateau, Bale Mountains National Park (9) (28667276343).jpg
location: Sanetti Plateau, Bale Mountains National Park
alt: An Ethiopian wolf standing in the grass of the Sanetti Plateau
caption: An Ethiopian wolf on the Sanetti Plateau, the world's rarest canid and found only in the Ethiopian highlands. Seeing one is the wildlife highlight of the Bale leg.

commonsFile: File:Lalibela, chiesa di bete medhane alem, esterno 04,0.jpg
alt: Colonnaded exterior of the rock-hewn church of Bete Medhane Alem in Lalibela
caption: Bete Medhane Alem, the largest monolithic rock-hewn church in the world and part of the Lalibela complex. It shows the scale and craftsmanship that defines the Lalibela visit.

location: Chennek camp area, Simien Mountains National Park
alt: Gelada baboons grazing in grassland near Chennek in the Simien Mountains
caption: Gelada baboons grazing near Chennek in the Simien Mountains, a camp stop on the trek. Walking among them is one of the trip's wildlife highlights.
